With several words, every word has to appear, each in any of them and in any order: Freiburg morning finds the morning runs from Freiburg. Escape closes the search bar.

Distances can be typed into the search box too (in km, with . or , for decimals); the other words are still searched for:

Type Finds activities of 10km or 10 km about 10 km (±5 %) >21 or >=21 at least 21 km <5km or <=5 at most 5 km 10-15km 10 to 15 km

A number without km or </> (like 2024) is searched for as text. Together with a distance range from Filter, both apply: <15km with a filter from 5 to 20 km shows 5 to 15 km.

Filter opens a dialog with ranges for Date, Distance (km), Duration (min) and Elevation (m), each with From and To. Leave a field empty to not filter by it. Both ends are included; a To below its From is raised to the From. Apply sets the filter. The active filters show as small labels next to the search box, and Reset clears the search text and all filters.

The info cards, the training calendar and the table all follow the search and the filters.

docs.title: Details panel
docs.text:
The details panel shows the activity you clicked, or else the latest activity of the sport shown. From top to bottom:

  • Overview: title, date and time, the type, the place it started in (once looked up), Duration, Pace (/km), for runs and walks GAP (/km) (the grade-adjusted pace), the route map, Distance and Elevation. The button at the top right opens the detail window. Hover the route to get a button that saves it as an image (PNG or SVG, white lines on a transparent background). If the activity came from or went to Garmin Connect, a line says so, with a button that opens it there.
  • Goals, sessions and trophies: a star with the number of goals the activity hit, the kind of training session it did, and a trophy with the number of segments where it is in the top 3. Hover them for the details. The box is left out when there is none of them.
  • Photos, comment and summary: the number of photos and the start of the comment and the AI summary. Click it to open the detail window, where they are in full.
  • Weather: the conditions, the average temperature, the strongest wind and the rain.
  • Best segments: the fastest pace over set distances within the activity (1, 5, 10, 21 and 42 km for runs; 5 to 200 km for rides; 1 to 50 km for walks).

Which boxes are shown can be chosen separately for runs, rides and walks in Settings on the Activity panel page: Route map, Garmin Connect link, Goals, sessions and trophies, Photos, comment and summary, Weather and Best segments. The same choice applies to the overview in the detail window (except photos, comment and summary, which only show in the details panel). Other activity types show every box.

docs.title: Deleting
docs.text: Choose Delete… in a row's ⋮ menu and confirm. The activity is removed with everything that belongs to it: its archived file (and the original kept by a fix), splits, weather, best performances, segment passes, heat-map track, AI summary and Garmin link, and the photos and videos copied into RunningMate. Linked photos and videos stay where they are; only the link to them is removed. Goals and the distance of its shoe or bike are updated, and a training session it was linked to stays in the plan, unlinked. Segments drawn on the activity are kept. Deleting can't be undone.

docs.title: Segments
docs.text: A segment is a stretch of road or trail you want to compare yourself on, for example a hill you run up every week. You mark segments on the map of an activity and the app finds every time you passed over them: in all activities already imported and in every activity imported later, for the same sport.

docs.title: Creating a segment
docs.text:
Open an activity, go to its Segments page in the detail window and click New segment. Click on the track where the segment starts, then where it ends; arrows along the track show the direction you went. Where the track passes the same spot more than once, the start is the first pass and the end the next pass after the start. Use the slider to fine-tune both ends, check distance, average grade, elevation gain and the elevation profile, give the segment a title and click Save segment. A segment must be at least 100 m long.

The app then looks for passes over the new segment in all your activities of the same sport, in the background.

docs.title: How a pass is found
docs.text:
An activity counts as a try when its track

  • comes within about 35 m of the segment's start and, later, of its end,
  • covers between 80 % and 125 % of the segment's length in between, and
  • stays within about 50 m of the segment all the way.

Passing in the opposite direction, taking a parallel road or a shortcut doesn't count. If you pass a segment several times in one activity (laps), every pass is a try of its own. Passes across a clock running backwards and impossible paces (faster than the per-point limit of the sport) are left out, as for the best segments.

The time of a pass is measured between the points closest to the segment's start and end. Recording pauses on the segment count towards the time.

Passes are looked for again whenever an activity is imported, re-imported or its route is fixed on the Fix data page.

docs.title: The Segments page
docs.text:
Open it from the sidebar or with ⇧⌘G. Segments are shown as cards, grouped by sport, each with a small map, the distance, average grade, climb and number of tries. Below these, the card lists the three fastest passes, your latest pass and your fastest pass this year (Best this year), each with its time and place overall.

Search by title with Search segments, and show only one sport with the buttons beside it.

docs.title: A segment
docs.text:
Click a card to open the segment. The header shows the title, the sport and when the segment was created.

Overview shows a map, the elevation profile with the grade, and the distance, average and steepest grade (Max grade, measured over 100 m so GPS noise doesn't make spikes), elevation gain, the lowest and highest point and the number of tries (with the number of activities, if you passed more than once in one). Below are the same highlights as on the card, and the full ranking: every pass, fastest first, with date, activity, time, pace (speed for rides) and heart rate, 20 per page.

Progress charts every pass by date with its time: the three fastest in gold, silver and bronze, the latest outlined, and the best time as a dashed line. Hover over a point to see its place.

On the Segments page, click a row of the ranking, a highlight or a point of the chart to open that activity. When you open a segment from an activity's Segments page, that activity's passes are marked in the ranking, which opens on the page of its first pass.

Compare opens the Compare page with the activities of the fastest passes (one per activity, ten at most), limited to the segment's stretch of each.

Click the pencil beside the title to rename the segment. Delete segment removes the segment and its ranking; the activities stay as they are.

docs.title: Trophies
docs.text: An activity that is among the three fastest passes on a segment shows a trophy with the number of such segments, on the dashboard feed and in the activity panel (e.g. "2 × Top 3"). On the activity's Segments page and in the rankings, a gold, silver or bronze trophy marks the place. Ranks are always current: when a faster pass is imported, or an activity is deleted, the places move.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The Settings dialog holds the settings for the app itself. Your profile, heart-rate zones, shoes and bikes are in the user settings. Open it with Settings at the bottom of the sidebar, with RunningMate → Settings… or with ⌘,. Changes are saved as soon as you make them. They are stored in ~/RunningData/appdata/settings.json.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
• Language: English or Deutsch. The language is also used for the titles of newly imported activities. Français can be chosen, but the app is shown in English then.
  • Appearance: Follow the system, Light or Dark.
  • Adding photos and videos from files: what happens when you add a photo or video from disk to an activity. Always copy into RunningMate copies the file into ~/RunningData/media. Always link to the originals keeps only a link to the file where it is, so it takes no extra space, but the photo is gone from RunningMate if you move or delete the file. Ask each time asks when you add files, with Remember my choice (can be changed in the settings) to set this setting from there. Photos from the Photos library are always copied.
  • Look up place names: names the town and part of town each activity started in (for example "Freiburg im Breisgau, Wiehre"), shown in the activity panel, the detail window and the Location column, and found by the search. On by default. It sends the coordinates of the start, and nothing else, to nominatim.openstreetmap.org, OpenStreetMap's place-name service: one activity a second at most, each only once (activities starting close to one already named reuse its name without asking). New activities are looked up after the import, older ones in the background. Turn it off to send nothing; names already found are kept. Names are in the language set when they were looked up.

docs.title: Activity panel
docs.text:
Choose which boxes the panel beside the activity list and the detail window show, separately for Runs, Rides and Walks. Tick or untick a box per sport:

  • Route map
  • Garmin Connect link
  • Goals, sessions and trophies
  • Photos, comment and summary (only beside the activity list)
  • Weather
  • Best segments

Other activities always show every box.

docs.title: AI summary
docs.text:
RunningMate can write a short summary of each activity with a language model that runs on your own computer, through Ollama. It is off until you turn it on.

  1. Install Ollama and a model, for example with ollama pull qwen2.5:7b.
  2. Tick Write activity summaries with a local AI model.
  3. Ollama server is http://localhost:11434 by default. Change it only if Ollama runs elsewhere.
  4. Click Load models. If none are installed, you are told so.
  5. Pick a Model. Models with 7 to 14 billion parameters (for example qwen2.5:14b) work well.
  6. Compare with the last sets how many weeks before the activity it is compared with: 2, 4 (the default), 8 or 12 weeks.

Nothing is sent to an online service: the facts go only to the Ollama server you entered, which with the default address is your own computer.

docs.title: The summary card
docs.text:
With summaries on and a model chosen, the General page of the detail window shows a Summary card, and the activity panel shows its start under Photos, comment and summary.

New activities from the last 14 days get a summary after they are imported. For other activities click Write summary; Rewrite writes a new one. Re-importing an activity drops its summary, since it was written from the old values; an activity from the last 14 days gets a new one.

RunningMate works out the comparison itself and gives the model only the results; the model is told not to calculate anything. The facts are:

  • the activity: sport, title, your comment, date, distance, time, pace or speed, heart rate, climb and temperature
  • how it compares with your last 10 activities over a similar distance (within 10 %, at least 0.5 km)
  • how it compares with your activities in the chosen weeks before it
  • where available: pacing over the splits, training effect, time in the heart-rate zones, your training form and personal bests set in the activity

The summary is 4 to 6 sentences in your language, says what stands out and ends with a hint for the next training. Below it you see which model wrote it. AI can be wrong.

The same setting turns on the AI notes on the Training page.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Shows the Data folder (RunningData in your home directory), how many Photos and videos are copied there and how much space they take, the Activity files (TCX, GPX), the archived file of each activity (with the GPX file it was converted from, if any) and how much space they take together with the originals kept when you fixed an activity and the files waiting for a route, and the Total size of the folder. All data stays on this computer. The folder is shared with the earlier Python version of RunningMate. See Sync for what is kept where.

docs.title: Photo size
docs.text:
Photos copied into RunningMate (from the Photos library, the photo picker, dropped onto the app or added from disk with Copy into RunningMate) are scaled down so their longest side fits the chosen size, and saved as JPEG. They are never scaled up, and turned upright first, so they keep their orientation; the capture date and the other photo details stay in the file. A photo that wouldn't come out noticeably smaller (by at least a tenth) is kept as it is, and so is one that can't be read. Linked photos and videos are never changed. PNG images with transparent areas stay PNG; HEIC photos are converted on macOS only.

Setting Longest side JPEG quality Size per photo¹ Good for Recommended (default) 2560 px 85 about 0.7–2.5 MB Full screen on a Retina laptop, the gallery, sharing Large 3840 px 90 about 2–5.5 MB Full screen on a 4K or 5K display Small 1920 px 80 about 0.4–1.3 MB A Full HD screen and the gallery, the least space Original unchanged unchanged about 2–8 MB Keeping the photos exactly as taken

¹ Measured on 12-megapixel phone photos (4032 × 3024 px); detailed photos (grass, gravel, leaves) are at the top of the range, sky and water at the bottom. Photos already smaller than the setting stay about the same size.

The setting applies to photos added from then on. Shrink stored photos… below it says how many of the photos already copied into RunningMate are larger than the setting and how much space they take, and after you confirm replaces them by smaller versions, a few at a time with progress. A HEIC or PNG photo becomes a .jpg file. Linked photos and their originals stay untouched. Replacing can't be undone, so keep the originals elsewhere (e.g. in your Photos library) if you may need them at full size again.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
The Sync dialog is where activities come in, and where they go out to Garmin Connect. Open it with Sync in the sidebar, with File → Sync… or with ⌘O. It opens on the source you used last.

On the left you pick the source:

  • Garmin Connect: imports new Garmin activities and uploads activities from elsewhere.
  • Folder sync: imports new TCX and GPX files from a folder.
  • TCX / GPX files: imports files you pick.

Strava and other services aren't supported yet.

docs.title: TCX / GPX files
docs.text: Click Choose TCX or GPX files… and pick one or more .tcx or .gpx files. The files are copied into RunningMate's archive; the originals stay where they are.

docs.title: Folder sync
docs.text:
Use this for a folder that another app exports to, for example an iCloud folder of RunGap or HealthFit. Click Choose… to pick the folder. Below it you see Last sync and how many new files are in the folder: TCX and GPX files changed since the last sync (on the first sync, all of them). Only the folder itself is read, not its subfolders. Click Sync (the button shows the number of files) to import them.

Files in iCloud Drive may have to be downloaded first. While that happens the progress line shows Reading files… 3 of 40 with the current file name.

docs.title: Garmin Connect
docs.text:
Sign in with your Garmin E-mail address and Password. If your account uses two-step verification, Garmin sends you a code; enter it under Verification code and click Confirm. Your password only goes to Garmin. RunningMate keeps a sign-in token in the system keychain, not the password. If Garmin stops accepting the token, the sign-in form comes back. Sign out forgets the token.

Import from Garmin Connect shows when the last sync ran and on which day the next one starts. Sync now downloads the activities from that day on and imports them. The first sync fetches your whole history. Activities that are already in RunningMate from another source (same day, about the same distance) are skipped before they are downloaded.

Upload to Garmin Connect sends activities that didn't come from Garmin, for example runs recorded with another app. Set Activities since (30 days ago at first) and click Upload. The button shows how many activities will go up: those since that date that weren't imported from Garmin and weren't uploaded before. Garmin skips activities it already has.

docs.title: Limiting the period
docs.text:
Every source has optional From and To dates. With dates set, only activities in that period are imported; Any time clears them. Without dates:

  • Folder sync imports every new file.
  • Garmin Connect imports everything since the last sync.

After a folder sync or Garmin sync with dates, the next sync still starts where the last complete one ended, so nothing in between is skipped. The same holds when a sync is cancelled or a file fails: the folder sync time only advances after a complete sync without dates or failures, and the next Garmin sync starts no later than the oldest failed download.

In all cases the newest activities are imported first, so you see this week's runs right away while older ones follow.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
A bar and a list show each file as it is done:

  • imported
  • Already imported: a file with the same name was imported before. A run exported as both TCX and GPX counts as the same file.
  • Already there (same day and distance): an activity on the same day with about the same distance (within 1 %, at least 50 m) exists, for example the same run recorded by your watch and your phone. The file is not imported.
  • No GPS: draw its route under Waiting for a route (see below)
  • failed, with the reason

At the end you get a summary such as "12 imported · 3 already imported · 0 failed". Cancel stops after the current file; what was imported so far stays. While a sync runs, the dialog can't be closed and you can't switch sources.

docs.title: Files without GPS
docs.text: A file with times but no GPS positions, such as a treadmill run or a watch with GPS off, isn't imported straight away. It is listed under Waiting for a route at the bottom of the Sync dialog, with its date, sport, duration and the distance the device measured. Click Draw route, then click the route you ran on the map, from start to finish, and save. Only then does it become an activity, with the same duplicate check as above. The bin icon removes a file from the list. Drawing on the map works as in the route fix editor of the detail window.

docs.title: After the import
docs.text:
Each new activity is computed from its file: distance, pace, heart rate, splits, best efforts, segments and so on. See Activity data for how. Then, without holding up the import:

  • The weather of the day is fetched from Open-Meteo for the place halfway along the route. This needs an internet connection.
  • The name of the place the activity started in (town and part of town) is looked up at Nominatim, unless turned off in the settings. Lookups run one after another, at most one a second, so after a large import the names fill in over a while; activities imported earlier are caught up on the same way. Re-importing or fixing an activity looks the name up again if its start moved.
  • If AI summaries are turned on in the settings, a summary is written for activities from the last 14 days. Older ones, for example when you import your whole history, get one only when you ask for it.

Goals, segments and training sessions pick up the new activities right away.

docs.title: Where things are kept
docs.text:
Everything lives in the RunningData folder in your home directory:

Path What it holds running_data.db The database with all activities and computed values. imports/ One archive per activity, {name}.tcx.tar.gz, holding the TCX file. A GPX file is converted to TCX for this; the original GPX is kept in the same archive. imports/{name}.orig.tcx.tar.gz The original file of an activity you fixed in the detail window, kept so you can reset to it. imports/pending/ Files waiting for a route. media/ Photos and videos copied into RunningMate, photos scaled down to the photo size. appdata/settings.json The settings. appdata/sync.json The sync folder and the last folder and Garmin sync.

The archives are what RunningMate goes back to when an activity is recomputed, so don't delete the imports folder.

docs.title: Training
docs.text: A training plan gets you to a target over a number of weeks: a race (5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon or any other distance, with an optional target time), getting in shape, or more fitness. The plan is built from fixed rules modelled on common running plans (Daniels, Pfitzinger, Higdon), starting from your runs of the last 6 months. Plans are for running only: rides and walks don't count.

docs.title: Making a plan
docs.text:
Open the Training page from the sidebar or with ⇧⌘T and click New training plan. The wizard has three steps.

  1. Training for: A race, Get in shape (mostly easy runs and one faster run a week) or More fitness (intervals and tempo runs). For a race, pick the Distance: 5 km, 10 km, Half marathon, Marathon or Other distance (1 to 100 km). Target time (optional), as H:MM:SS, sets the race pace; without it the pace comes from your runs.
  2. Start, Weeks, Training days and Long run: the first day (the next Monday unless you change it), the number of weeks (4, 6, 8, 3 months, 16, or any number from 1 to 52), the weekdays you can train and the day of the long run, one of your training days. A race is on the long-run day of the last week. Name is optional; left empty, the plan is named after its target, for example "10 km in 0:45:00".

  3. Preview: Your last 6 months shows what the plan starts from (km a week lately, runs a week, longest run, VO2max), then the number of sessions, the end date, your easy and threshold paces, and the plan week by week with its phase, its km and a bar per session. Warnings show up above it:

    • the plan is shorter than usual for the distance (4 weeks for up to 6 km, 6 for up to 12 km, 8 for up to 25 km, 12 beyond);
    • you ran less than half of what the distance usually builds on (10, 15, 20 or 30 km a week); the plan starts gently;
    • there are too few runs to work out paces, so the sessions only have distances;
    • the target time needs a VO2max more than 5 above your current one; training starts from where you are.

    Tick Also set a goal to create a matching goal on the Goals page: for a race, the race distance in one run by the race day (within the target time, if you gave one); otherwise the plan's average weekly km every week until the plan ends.

Click Create plan to save it.

docs.title: How plans are built
docs.text: The plan is worked out from your runs by fixed rules, so the preview in the wizard is the plan you get. No AI is involved.

docs.title: Where it starts
docs.text:
• Volume: the km you ran per week over the last 8 weeks, or 80 % of your weekly km over the last 26 weeks when that is more, and at least 10 km.
  • Longest run: the longest run of the last 8 weeks (of the last 26 when there was none), and at least 5 km.
  • VO2max: the higher of the estimate from your whole runs and the one from your fastest stretch of 3 km or more (a best effort) in the last 26 weeks. Without either, the VO2max from your profile is used. With a target time, training paces come from the lower of your current VO2max and the one the target time needs.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
• A race plan ends with a Taper: one week for races up to 12 km, two for longer ones. The weeks before it are split into Base (about 40 %), Build (about 40 %) and Peak (about 20 %).
  • Get in shape and More fitness plans have three building weeks and an Easier week, again and again.

docs.title: Weekly volume
docs.text:
• The km grow by at most 10 % a week, up to a peak: 1.5 times the starting volume (1.3 times for Get in shape), and never more than 35 km a week for races up to 6 km, 45 km up to 12 km, 55 km up to 25 km and 70 km beyond.
  • Every fourth week is easier, at 75 % of the week before. Building goes on from where it left off afterwards.
  • The taper cuts the km: one taper week to 60 %; two taper weeks to 75 % and then 55 %.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
• Long run, at easy pace on the long-run day: about 30 % of the week's km (35 % for a half marathon, 42 % for a marathon, 5 points more with three training days or fewer). It grows by at most 2 km a week over your longest run so far and stops at 14 km for races up to 6 km, 17 km up to 12 km, 21 km up to 25 km, 32 km beyond, 16 km for Get in shape and 18 km for More fitness. It is always the longest session of the week.
  • Hard sessions (Tempo run or Intervals): none with one training day, one with two or three days, two with four or more. Base and taper weeks and all Get in shape weeks have at most one, easier weeks none. They go on the days farthest from the long run, never the day before or after it or another hard session. Each has a warm-up and cool-down of a quarter of the week's km (2 to 3.5 km), and its work stays within 20 % of the week's km and shorter than the long run; repetitions are cut to fit.
  • Easy runs share the rest of the week's km, at least 3 km each; when there isn't enough for all training days, some days stay free. The run on the day after the long run is a Recovery run, 80 % as long and a little slower.
  • Race week: up to three short recovery runs (3 to 6 km) before the race, not on the day before, then the Race on the long-run day. Nothing after it.

Hard sessions get longer through each phase:

Plan and week First hard session Second hard session Get in shape 3 to 5 × 4 min at threshold pace – More fitness 5 to 8 × 800 m at interval pace 2 to 3 × 10 min at threshold pace Race, base 2 to 3 × 8 to 10 min at threshold pace – Race, build 3 to 4 × 10 min at threshold pace 5 to 6 × 1 km at interval pace¹ Race, peak 4 to 5 × 1600 m at race pace¹ 20 min at threshold pace Race, taper 4 × 1 km at race pace¹ –

¹ For races over 12 km: build 2 to 3 × 3 km at marathon pace, peak 2 to 3 × 4 km at race pace, taper 3 × 2 km at race pace. The rest between repetitions is 2 minutes, 3 for 1 km, 1600 m and 2 km repetitions.

docs.title: Paces
docs.text:
Paces come from your VO2max after Jack Daniels' tables, each a range in min/km:

  • Easy: 62 to 70 % of VO2max, for easy and long runs. Recovery runs go from 10 s/km faster to 20 s/km slower than the slow end of easy pace.
  • Marathon pace: your predicted marathon pace, ±5 s/km.
  • Threshold: 86 to 89 % of VO2max, for tempo runs.
  • Interval: 96 to 99 % of VO2max.
  • Race pace: the target time divided by the distance, or else the time predicted from your VO2max, ±3 s/km.

Without a VO2max and without a target time, sessions only have distances.

docs.title: Following the plan
docs.text:
The Training page shows the selected plan with its state (Upcoming, Active or Finished), its target and dates, the badge of its matching goal, and Sessions with a run, Done as planned, Missed, the Distance done and planned, and your paces. A coloured strip shows the phases. With several plans, pick one from the row at the top; Show archived includes archived plans.

Below come the plan's weeks as rows of seven days, with the phase and the km done and planned per week, the current week highlighted, and a card per session with what it asks for and, once done or past, how it went. Click a session to change its Kind, Date, Distance, Pace (fastest and slowest), and for tempo runs and intervals the Repetitions, Minutes each or Metres each and Rest (s), or to add a Note. Skip marks it as skipped (Not skipped undoes it), and the bin deletes it. Hover a day and click + to add a session.

Adapt plan rebuilds the sessions from today on from your recent runs. It goes on with 1.1 times your weekly km of the last 3 weeks (at least 10 km), never with more than the plan had for this week, and from your current longest run and VO2max. Sessions before today stay, and so do sessions you changed, skipped, linked to a run or set to have no run. It isn't available once a plan is finished.

From the plan's buttons you can also Rename, Archive (Restore) or delete a plan. Deleting removes the plan and its sessions; your runs and a matching goal stay.

The dashboard shows the sessions of this week and next week in a row below the goals; click one to open the Training page. In the four-week calendar, days with a session get a ring: dashed in the session's colour while ahead, in the colour of how it went once done or past. Both move with the dashboard's date arrows.

docs.title: Matching runs to sessions
docs.text:
Every run is matched to a session automatically: a run on the session's day first, otherwise one on the day before or after that no other session took; between two runs, the one closer to the planned distance. In the session window, under Run, you can link another run from the three days either side by hand, choose No run for this session, or go back with Match automatically. An activity that did a session shows a small calendar mark in the dashboard feed and the activity panel, in the colour of how it went; hover it for the plan, the kind of session and the result.

Each session gets a verdict:

  • Done as planned: at least 80 % of the planned distance, and not harder or easier than planned. A race counts as done from 97 % of its distance, as GPS measures a little short.
  • Harder than planned: an easy, recovery or long run more than 10 s/km faster than easy pace, an easy or recovery run more than 30 % longer than planned, or an average heart rate above zone 2 (once your heart-rate zones are saved in the profile).
  • Easier than planned: the fastest kilometres of a tempo or interval run (as many as its work) more than 15 s/km slower than the slow end of its pace.
  • Partly done: less than 80 % of the planned distance.
  • Missed: a past session without a run that wasn't skipped.
  • Skipped: a session you skipped.

The pace of a run is its moving pace, without pauses. Matching is worked out from your runs each time, so importing, editing or deleting a run updates it right away.

docs.title: AI coach
docs.text: With AI turned on in the settings (a local Ollama model), the Training page has a This week note: Explain has the model explain the current week of the plan. In the session window, once a run did the session, Comment has it comment on how the run went. Rewrite writes a note again. Notes are kept and marked with the model that wrote them. The plan doesn't need it: without a model these notes are just not shown.

docs.title: User Settings
docs.text: The user settings hold your profile, your heart-rate zones and your shoes and bikes. Open them with User at the bottom of the sidebar or with RunningMate → User Profile…. Pick a page on the left. Heart rate zones, Shoes and Bikes become available once you have saved a profile.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Fill in the fields and click Save.

  • Name
  • Birthday, as DD.MM.YYYY. Your age is calculated from it, for the suggested heart-rate zones and for rating your cardio fitness.
  • Weight (kg), between 20 and 300. Used for the calories and the power estimate of each activity.
  • Height (cm), between 100 and 250.
  • Resting heart rate (bpm), between 30 and 120. Used for the heart-rate zones with the Karvonen method.
  • Maximum heart rate (bpm), between 100 and 230 and above the resting heart rate. Used for the suggested heart-rate zones and the zones worked out from it.
  • Sex, optional. Only used to compare your cardio fitness (VO2max) with people of your age and sex.

A changed weight applies to activities imported or recomputed afterwards.

docs.title: Heart rate zones
docs.text:
First pick how the five zones are set under Method:

  • Custom: you enter the upper bound of each zone in bpm. The lower bound of each zone is shown next to it: zone 1 starts at half the upper bound of zone 5, every other zone one beat above the previous one. Each bound must be a whole number between 40 and 240 and above the previous one. As long as you haven't saved bounds, the page suggests some: 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 % of your maximum heart rate, or of 220 minus your age if you haven't entered one. Adjust them and click Save.
  • Percent of maximum heart rate: the zones end at 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 % of the maximum heart rate from your profile; zone 1 starts at 50 %.
  • Karvonen (heart-rate reserve): the same shares, but of the range between your resting and maximum heart rate, added to the resting heart rate.

For the last two the page shows the resulting zones in bpm; you can't edit them. They follow your profile: change your resting or maximum heart rate there and the zones change with it. Without a maximum heart rate (and, for Karvonen, a resting heart rate) in the profile the page asks you to enter them and you can't save the method. Your custom bounds are kept when you switch to another method, so switching back brings them back.

Until zones are saved, no time in zones is shown. With zones, you see Time in heart-rate zones on the Heart rate zones page of the detail window and on the Health Data page. In the Heart-rate trend on that page, the tops of zones 1, 3 and 5 are drawn as Min, Ideal and Max lines. See Heart rate zones for the methods and how the time in zones is worked out.

VO2max is your own value, if you know it (for example from a lab test or your watch). It is used where RunningMate can't estimate one from your runs.

docs.title: Shoes and Bikes
docs.text:
Shoes are for runs and walks, bikes for rides. Each page lists your items with their Distance (km) and an In use switch.

  • Add an item with a name (and, for a bike, an optional Weight (kg)) and click Add. It starts at 0 km.
  • Assign it to an activity on the Edit page of the detail window, under Shoes or Bike. New activities get none; you pick it per activity. The change applies right away and moves the activity's distance from the previous item to the new one.
  • The distance follows the activities: editing an activity's distance, re-importing it or deleting it adds or takes off the difference.
  • Switch In use off for shoes or bikes you've retired. They keep their distance but aren't offered for new activities.
  • Deleting an item removes it from every activity it was assigned to. To keep the history, switch In use off instead.
